newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Cash woes may hurt Russian grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Cash woes may hurt Russian grain harvest.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
CASH PROBLEMS COULD HAMPER RUSSIAN HARVEST PROSPECTS
MOSCOW, July 28 - By July 21, Russian farms had threshed about 3.0 million hectares, compared to 2.8 million hectares at this time last year.
Current average grain yields are 2.66 tonnes per hectare (bunker weight), up six percent on last year.
Though Russian officials expect 1997 grain output to rise to up to 80 million tonnes (1996: 69.3 million tonnes), there are some factors which may affect the outcome.

As usual, the government has not mobilized adequate finances for the harvest. Due to low demand, the Finance Ministry's sales of "agricultural bonds" have raised only 0.5 trillion rubles, a mere one quarter of the target.
Furthermore, only 52 percent of grain combines were ready for fieldwork by July 1.
These reasons may slow down harvesting and cause additional losses.
For all these reasons, SovEcon's forecast for Russia's total grain output remains unchanged in the range of 71-76 million tonnes.
